The soleplate is visible at the bottom, appearing metallic grey. A power cord extends from the rear left. The background consists of white, wrinkled fabric, likely a shirt or sheet.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The temperature dial and buttons are not distinct geometric objects; they appear fused into the main body casing with soft, undefined edges, lacking the crisp separation of real mechanical parts.
The metal surface is unnaturally smooth and lacks the micro-texture or specific hole patterns (steam vents) found on real irons, resembling a simple grey gradient rather than engineered metal.
The connection between the power cord and the body, as well as the heel rest structure, appears slightly warped and lacks clear mechanical joints, blending softly into the background.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is correctly classified as an iron and not a similar-looking appliance or abstract shape.
To rigorously analyze the 'melted' appearance of the controls and the lack of texture on the soleplate for signs of generation artifacts.
To check for boundary bleeding between the plastic body and the background, and to ensure the handle is a continuous loop.
To verify the spatial relationship between the vertical iron and the fabric background, ensuring no floating elements.

focus_areas: Definition of control dials/buttons (are they distinct or melted?)
Presence of steam holes on the soleplate
Boundary sharpness between the iron and the white fabric background
Structural integrity of the handle and heel rest
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'control panel' area. Real irons have distinct, raised buttons or dials. If the expert sees only smooth, amorphous bumps, this is a strong sign of AI generation failure (melting). Also, verify if the soleplate has ANY holes; a completely smooth metal plate is physically incorrect for a steam iron.
